Checked three ways: the snapshot's pixelContrast gives #6c757d on #dcdcdc, 3.42:1, 16px weight 400; the live CSS gives the same (Bootstrap .form-control::placeholder {color:#6c757d; opacity:1} and site.css 'div > div.form input, div > div.form textarea {background-color:#dcdcdc}'); and sampling the screenshot gives darkest glyph pixel #6c757d on #dcdcdc, 3.42:1. Normal-size text needs 4.5:1. The placeholder is the field's only visible label (no <label>, no aria-label), so it is information users need, not incidental text, and no 1.4.3 exception applies. It collects the user's own full name, a purpose listed in WCAG 2.1 section 7 (name), and the input has no autocomplete attribute, so the purpose is not programmatically determinable. claimTrue: yes, autocomplete is absent in the captured HTML, and the snapshot records Chromium's form issue FormInputAssignedAutocompleteValueToIdOrNameAttributeError for this field, so 'Chromium's form check flags this field' holds too. elementFails: yes, 1.3.5 applies (HTML supports autocomplete tokens) and the field gives no token; site.js only validates and posts the form and adds nothing. captureDiffers: no, the live HTML has the same input without autocomplete. The claim names the failure, so true_positive.

judgments.label: true_positive

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Element: the h2 "Estatística do Boldrini" (shown uppercase by CSS) at the top of the teal .stats band. Directly under it, in the same band, are a photo of a child and an infographic image with the hospital's statistics (20% convênio / 80% SUS, patients treated, cure rate, 80 beds, 90 doctors, 130 mil m²), as the screenshot and the snapshot's image data show. The heading describes that topic well, so it meets 2.4.6. The text that follows in document order before the next heading (testimonials, retinoblastoma screening, services) is a separate white section with no heading of its own; that missing heading is a structure issue (1.3.1, 2.4.10 AAA), not a fault of this heading. claimTrue: no, the content right under it is the statistics infographic. elementFails: no. captureDiffers: no, the live HTML has the same heading and images. The two images have no alt attribute, so the statistics exist only as pixels (a 1.1.1 failure for the infographic). A judgment working from the page text would see only the testimonials under the heading, hence context_missing.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Element: the link "boldrini.org.br/doacoes" (href="/doacoes") at the end of a paragraph in the teal box of the donations section. The link text is a URL, as the claim says (claimTrue: yes), but its purpose is clear from the text together with its programmatically determined context: the same sentence and paragraph read 'Seja sócio amigo do Boldrini: boldrini.org.br/doacoes', after text about the support of people and companies, and the path word 'doacoes' (donations) itself says where it goes. So it meets 2.4.4 (elementFails: no). captureDiffers: no, the live HTML has the same paragraph and link. The claim treats a URL as link text as a failure in itself and ignores the sentence that gives its purpose, a stricter rule than 2.4.4, so false_positive, criterion_misapplied.
